claim: The sarcomere is the smallest functional unit in striated muscle.
source: The sarcomere is the smallest functional unit in striated muscle.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about muscle structure.

claim: The cardiac sarcomere is composed of thick and thin filament proteins that work together to generate force and shorten the sarcomere, and regulate sarcomere contraction and relaxation in a Ca2+-dependent manner.
source: The cardiac sarcomere is composed of thick and thin filament proteins that work together to generate force and shorten the sarcomere, and regulate sarcomere contraction and relaxation in a Ca2+-dependent manner (Gordon et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gordon et al., 2000.

claim: The cardiac thick filament is composed of myosin II polymers accompanied by associated proteins, myosin-binding protein C (MyBP-C), titin, and obscurin.
source: The cardiac thick filament is composed of myosin II polymers accompanied by associated proteins, myosin-binding protein C (MyBP-C), titin, and obscurin (Gordon et al., 2000; Craig and Woodhead, 2006; Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gordon et al., 2000; Craig and Woodhead, 2006; Wang et al., 2018.

claim: The major proteins of the cardiac thin filament include F-actin-containing myosin-binding sites – tropomyosin (Tm) and the cardiac troponin complex (cTn).
source: The major proteins of the cardiac thin filament include F-actin-containing myosin-binding sites – tropomyosin (Tm) and the cardiac troponin complex (cTn) (Gordon et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gordon et al., 2000.

claim: Myosin molecules of the thick filaments are constituted of six noncovalently associated polypeptides: two heavy chains and four light chains (LCs).
source: Myosin molecules of the thick filaments are constituted of six noncovalently associated polypeptides: two heavy chains and four light chains (LCs).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about myosin structure.

claim: The paired, N-terminal heads of the two MHCs are positioned at the surface, facilitating interactions with actin filaments.
source: The paired, N-terminal heads of the two MHCs are positioned at the surface, facilitating interactions with actin filaments.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about myosin structure.

claim: Between the heads and the tail is a coiled-coil that makes up the myosin S2 rod segment.
source: Between the heads and the tail is a coiled-coil that makes up the myosin S2 rod segment.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about myosin structure.

claim: The neck region of myosin is the site of accessory protein binding that consists of two pairs of LCs: essential (ELC) and regulatory (RLC).
source: The neck region of myosin is the site of accessory protein binding that consists of two pairs of LCs: essential (ELC) and regulatory (RLC).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about myosin structure.

claim: Near the N-terminus, the individual MHC forms a distinct globular structure – myosin S1 fragment – that interacts with the actin filament in a cyclic fashion.
source: Near the N-terminus, the individual MHC forms a distinct globular structure – myosin S1 fragment – that interacts with the actin filament in a cyclic fashion (Geeves and Holmes, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Geeves and Holmes, 1999.

claim: Myosin binds to actin and ATP and undergoes several conformational changes that are essential to its function.
source: Myosin binds to actin and ATP and undergoes several conformational changes that are essential to its function: (1) actomyosin complex formation along with release of Pi and ADP from myosin cause a swinging motion during the force-generating powerstroke; (2) during rigor, ATP binding to myosin results in a reduction in actin affinity and dissociation of actomyosin; and (3) ATP hydrolysis occurs when myosin is dissociated from actin and primes the lever arm for the next cross-bridge cycle (Tang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tang et al., 2016.

claim: Post-translational modification (PTM) of myofilament proteins can regulate their mechanical properties and modulate cardiac sarcomere function.
source: Post-translational modification (PTM) of myofilament proteins can regulate their mechanical properties and modulate cardiac sarcomere function.
evidence: This is a general statement about PTMs supported by the broader literature context.

claim: PTMs have been shown to alter the canonical structure, function, localization, and half-life of modified sarcomeric proteins.
source: PTMs have been shown to alter the canonical structure, function, localization, and half-life of modified sarcomeric proteins (Mnatsakanyan et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mnatsakanyan et al., 2018.

claim: Both histone acetyltransferase (HAT; p300/CBP-associated factor [PCAF]) and histone deacetylase 4 (HDAC4) have been found localized in the sarcomeric matrix.
source: Both histone acetyltransferase (HAT; p300/CBP-associated factor [PCAF]) and histone deacetylase 4 (HDAC4) have been found localized in the sarcomeric matrix (Samant et al., 2015; Gupta et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Samant et al., 2015 and Gupta et al., 2008.

claim: HDAC6 has been shown to assume a sarcomeric localization.
source: Furthermore, HDAC6 has also been shown to assume a sarcomeric localization (Demos-Davies et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Demos-Davies et al., 2014.

claim: A number of sarcomeric proteins are phosphorylated, including MyBP-C, troponin T (TnT), and troponin I (TnI) by cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA), and myosin regulatory light chain (RLC) by myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK).
source: A number of sarcomeric proteins are phosphorylated, including MyBP-C, troponin T (TnT), and troponin I (TnI) by cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA), and myosin regulatory light chain (RLC) by myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK) (Sumandea and Steinberg, 2011; Colson et al., 2010; Seguchi et al., 2007; Chan et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sumandea and Steinberg, 2011; Colson et al., 2010; Seguchi et al., 2007; Chan et al., 2008.

claim: Several kinases are implicated in phosphorylation of striated muscle Tm, including tropomyosin kinase, PKA, and protein kinase Cζ.
source: Several kinases are implicated in phosphorylation of striated muscle Tm, including tropomyosin kinase, PKA, and protein kinase Cζ (Heeley et al., 1989; Mak et al., 1978; Montgomery and Mak, 1984; Reddy et al., 1973; Wu and Solaro, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Heeley et al., 1989; Mak et al., 1978; Montgomery and Mak, 1984; Reddy et al., 1973; Wu and Solaro, 2007.

claim: β-MHC, encoded by MYH7, is the predominant isoform of myosin in the adult human heart.
source: Remarkably absent from the list of phosphorylated sarcomeric proteins in human hearts is β-MHC, encoded by MYH7, the predominant isoform of myosin in the adult human heart.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about cardiac myosin isoforms.

claim: The massive size of β-MHC, ~223 kDa, imposes limitations with current technological approaches and challenges our ability to obtain complete sequence coverage.
source: The massive size of β-MHC, ~223 kDa, imposes limitations with current technological approaches and challenges our ability to obtain complete sequence coverage.
evidence: This is a statement about technical challenges in studying β-MHC.

claim: In a study by Kawai et al. examining PTMs on MYH6, the predominant murine myosin isoform, phosphorylation sites were identified in control hearts with a number of these residues not phosphorylated in HCM hearts.
source: In a study by Kawai et al. examining PTMs on MYH6, the predominant murine myosin isoform,(Zhang et al., 2020) phosphorylation sites were identified in control hearts with a number of these residues not phosphorylated in HCM hearts (Kawai et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2020 and Kawai et al., 2017.

claim: Jin et al. identified acetylated, methylated, and trimethylated residues in human β-MHC using size-exclusion chromatography (SEC)/middle-down mass spectrometry (MS).
source: In addition, Jin et al. identified acetylated, methylated, and trimethylated residues in human β-MHC using size-exclusion chromatography (SEC)/middle-down mass spectrometry (MS) (Jin et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jin et al., 2017.

claim: The patient groups from whom explanted heart tissues were collected included explanted hearts from healthy donors (nonfailing (NF)) and end-stage heart failure patients, who were reported to have either ischemic heart failure (I-HF) or non-ischemic heart failure (NI-HF).
source: The patient groups from whom explanted heart tissues were collected included explanted hearts from healthy donors (nonfailing (NF)) and end-stage heart failure patients, who were reported to have either ischemic heart failure (I-HF) or non-ischemic heart failure (NI-HF).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and patient groups used in the study.

claim: Patients' ages ranged from 41 to 69 years with each condition represented (NF, NI-HF, and I-HF).
source: Patients' ages ranged from 41 to 69 years with each condition represented (NF, NI-HF, and I-HF) (Supplementary file 1) and were similarly distributed among the three groups.
evidence: This describes demographic characteristics of the patient samples.

claim: K951-Ac was significantly reduced in both ischemic and nonischemic failing hearts compared to nondiseased hearts.
source: K951-Ac was significantly reduced in both ischemic and nonischemic failing hearts compared to nondiseased hearts.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations show that K951-Ac may impact stability of thick filament tail interactions and ultimately myosin head positioning.
source: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations show that K951-Ac may impact stability of thick filament tail interactions and ultimately myosin head positioning.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations performed in the study.

claim: K58-Ac altered the solvent-exposed SH3 domain surface – known for protein–protein interactions – but did not appreciably change motor domain conformation or dynamics under conditions studied.
source: K58-Ac altered the solvent-exposed SH3 domain surface – known for protein–protein interactions – but did not appreciably change motor domain conformation or dynamics under conditions studied.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations performed in the study.

claim: K213-Ac/T215-P altered loop 1's structure and dynamics – known to regulate ADP-release, ATPase activity, and sliding velocity.
source: Together, K213-Ac/T215-P altered loop 1's structure and dynamics – known to regulate ADP-release, ATPase activity, and sliding velocity.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations combined with established knowledge about loop 1 function.

claim: β-MHC acetylation levels may be influenced more by the PTM location than the type of heart disease since less protected acetylation sites are reduced in both heart failure groups.
source: Our study suggests that β-MHC acetylation levels may be influenced more by the PTM location than the type of heart disease since less protected acetylation sites are reduced in both heart failure groups.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data patterns observed in the study.

claim: These PTMs have potential to modulate interactions between β-MHC and other regulatory sarcomeric proteins, ADP-release rate of myosin, flexibility of the S2 region, and cardiac myofilament contractility in normal and failing hearts.
source: Additionally, these PTMs have potential to modulate interactions between β-MHC and other regulatory sarcomeric proteins, ADP-release rate of myosin, flexibility of the S2 region, and cardiac myofilament contractility in normal and failing hearts.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the MD simulation results and known functions of the modified regions.

claim: Six of the identified PTMs are distributed throughout the myosin motor domain and two within the tail.
source: Six of these PTMs are distributed throughout the myosin motor domain (Figure 4A) and two within the tail (Figure 4B).
evidence: This describes the spatial distribution of PTMs shown in Figure 4.

claim: The myosin motor is comprised of four domains: the N-terminal domain, the upper and lower 50 kDa domains, and the converter arranged around a central β-sheet.
source: The myosin motor is comprised of four domains: the N-terminal domain, the upper and lower 50 kDa domains, and the converter arranged around a central β-sheet (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about myosin structure, illustrated in Figure 4A.

claim: Residue K34 is located between the SH3-like domain and the converter domain.
source: Residue K34 is located between the SH3-like domain and the converter domain (Figure 4A).
evidence: This describes the structural location of K34 as shown in Figure 4A.

claim: K58 is located within the SH3-like domain, which typically serves as a module for protein–protein interactions.
source: K58 is located within the SH3-like domain, which typically serves as a module for protein–protein interactions.
evidence: This combines structural location data with established knowledge about SH3 domain function.

claim: Acetylation of either K34 or K58 may interfere with normal interactions of the SH3-like domain.
source: Therefore, it is anticipated that acetylation of either K34 or K58 may interfere with normal interactions of this domain.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the location of the PTMs.

claim: Residues S210, K213, and T215 are sequentially close in the primary structure, and they lie together on one face of the myosin motor domain near the ATP-binding pocket in a region called loop 1.
source: Residues S210, K213, and T215 are sequentially close in the primary structure, and it is interesting to note that they lie together on one face of the myosin motor domain near the ATP-binding pocket in a region called loop 1.
evidence: This describes the structural location of these residues.

claim: Loop 1 is notable for its influence on ATP/ADP cycling.
source: This loop is notable for its influence on ATP/ADP cycling (Murphy and Spudich, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Murphy and Spudich, 1998.

claim: Modifications at S210, K213, and T215 may influence ATP binding and/or Pi and ADP-release dynamics.
source: It is plausible, therefore, to expect that these modifications may influence ATP binding and/or Pi and ADP-release dynamics (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the location of the PTMs near the ATP-binding pocket.

claim: S210-P was found to exist as a single modification only.
source: S210-P was found to exist as a single modification only.
evidence: This is a finding from the mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: K213-Ac was only found coincident with phosphorylation of T215, but T215-P was also found on its own, without K213-Ac.
source: Although K213-Ac was only found coincident with phosphorylation of T215, T215-P was also found on its own, without K213-Ac.
evidence: This is a finding from the mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: The K213-Ac/T215-P-modified sequence (amino acids 207–234, m/z 766.36) was detectable as an isotope dot product (idotp) with a value below 0.5, and therefore was unquantifiable.
source: The K213-Ac/T215-P-modified sequence (amino acids 207–234, m/z 766.36) was detectable as an isotope dot product (idotp) with a value below 0.5, and therefore was unquantifiable (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: The acetylated residue K429 is located within the myosin head-like domain at the actin-binding interface.
source: The acetylated residue K429 is located within the myosin head-like domain at the actin-binding interface.
evidence: This describes the structural location of K429.

claim: The modified residues K951 and K1195 are located within the coiled-coil of the S2 region.
source: The remainder of the modified residues K951 and K1195 are located within the coiled-coil of the S2 region, although K1195 is missing from the model in Figure 4A.
evidence: This describes the structural location of K951 and K1195.

claim: The ratios of modified PTM sites were variable, ranging between 1 and 14 in the NF donor hearts, with a tendency for decreased abundance in failing hearts.
source: Overall, the ratios of modified PTM sites were variable, ranging between 1 and 14 in the NF donor hearts, with a tendency for decreased abundance in failing hearts.
evidence: This is a finding from the quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: PTM K951-Ac is significantly decreased with ratios of approximately 14 in control hearts and 5 in failing hearts.
source: Of interest is PTM K951-Ac as acetylation at this site is significantly decreased with ratios of approximately 14 in control hearts and 5 in failing hearts.
evidence: This is a finding from the quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: K1195 follows the same trend as K951-Ac (but not statistically significant) in the tail region.
source: Following the same trend (but not statistically significant) is K1195 also in the tail region.
evidence: This is a finding from the quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: K34-Ac and K429-Ac are found in the myosin motor domain where they may be protected from HDAC activity.
source: Both K34-Ac and K429-Ac are found in the myosin motor domain where they may be protected from HDAC activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural location of these PTMs.

claim: K429-Ac is a low-abundance PTM with ratios of modified peptides/IRP ratios of approximately 1 and 1.4.
source: K429-Ac is a low-abundance PTM with ratios of modified peptides/IRP ratios of approximately 1 and 1.4.
evidence: This is a finding from the quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: K429-Ac is buried within the actin-binding cleft and may have been modified prior to protein folding.
source: This site is buried within the actin-binding cleft and may have been modified prior to protein folding.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the structural location of K429.

claim: K34-Ac is more abundant with approximate modified peptide ratios of 5–10.
source: K34-Ac, on the other hand, is more abundant with approximate modified peptide ratios of 5–10.
evidence: This is a finding from the quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: K58-Ac may be more susceptible to removal by HDACs or lower HAT activity under I-HF conditions.
source: Perhaps the most interesting observation can be made for the co-modified peptide containing K58-Ac as it may be more susceptible to removal by HDACs or lower HAT activity under I-HF conditions.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed reduction in K58-Ac in I-HF samples.

claim: The average ratios of T215-P ranged from 3 to 2, while in the control nondiseased hearts the modification was nearly undetectable in two samples.
source: The average ratios of T215-P ranged from 3 to 2, while in the control nondiseased hearts the modification was nearly undetectable in two samples.
evidence: This is a finding from the quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: S210 on peptide 6 had ratios of approximately 1–2 modified peptide/IRP in all groups.
source: Another phosphorylated residue was the phospho-serine at S210 on peptide 6, with ratios of approximately 1–2 modified peptide/IRP in all groups.
evidence: This is a finding from the quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: T215 on peptide 7 had ratios of approximately 1–2 of the modified peptides/IRP in all the groups.
source: T215 on peptide 7 had ratios of approximately 1–2 of the modified peptides/IRP in all the groups (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a finding from the quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: Three modifications – at the lateral face of the myosin motor domain – have potential importance due to their proximity to the ATP-binding pocket: (1) S210-P (single), (2) T215-P (single), and (3) K213-Ac plus T215-P (double).
source: When examining the 3D structure of the β-MHC motor domain, we observed three modifications – at the lateral face of the myosin motor domain – with potential importance due to their proximity to the ATP-binding pocket: (1) S210-P (single), (2) T215-P (single), and (3) K213-Ac plus T215-P (double).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural location of these PTMs.

claim: Lys 951 is located in S2 within the myosin tail.
source: Lys 951 is located in S2 within the myosin tail (Figure 4).
evidence: This describes the structural location of K951 as shown in Figure 4.

claim: In mature myosin, the tail forms a coiled-coil structure where the helical tails of two MHCs are wrapped around one another.
source: In mature myosin, the tail forms a coiled-coil structure where the helical tails of two MHCs are wrapped around one another.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about myosin structure.

claim: Archetypal coiled-coil helices have a conserved sequence repeat of seven amino acids: positions a–g in which positions a and d are hydrophobic residues that form a 'knobs in holes' interlocking structure that promotes a well-packed hydrophobic core.
source: Archetypal coiled-coil helices have a conserved sequence repeat of seven amino acids: positions a–g in which positions a and d are hydrophobic residues that form a 'knobs in holes' interlocking structure that promotes a well-packed hydrophobic core (Truebestein and Leonard, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Truebestein and Leonard, 2016.

claim: Myosin tails generally follow the archetypal coiled-coil pattern, but there are a small number of 'skip' residues that intermittently disrupt the heptad repeat pattern and increase local flexibility into the tail by weakening interactions in the hydrophobic core of the thick filament.
source: Myosin tails generally follow this archetypal pattern, but there are a small number of 'skip' residues that intermittently disrupt the heptad repeat pattern and increase local flexibility into the tail by weakening interactions in the hydrophobic core of the thick filament (Taylor et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Taylor et al., 2015.

claim: In implicit solvent MD, the simulated S2 fragment was flexible, with larger magnitude Cα RMSDs associated with bending of the tail.
source: In implicit solvent MD, the simulated S2 fragment was flexible (Table 4), larger magnitude Cα RMSDs were associated with bending of the tail.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: The coiled-coil structure was largely preserved in the unmodified simulations.
source: Although bending occurred, the coiled-coil structure was largely preserved in the unmodified simulations (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Some coiled-coil structure was lost in the K951-Ac simulations in the vicinity of the modification site.
source: Some coiled-coil structure was lost in the K951-Ac simulations in the vicinity of the modification site (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations shown in Figure 7B.

claim: In simulations without PTMs, K951 formed transient interactions with E949 of the opposite chain, but most interactions made by K951 were hydrophobic and involved L950 of the opposite chain.
source: In simulations without PTMs, K951 formed transient interactions with E949 of the opposite chain, but most interactions made by K951 were hydrophobic and involved L950 of the opposite chain (Figure 7A and C).
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations shown in Figure 7A and C.

claim: Acetylation of K951 altered contacts made by K951: the frequency of salt bridge formation with Glu residues was diminished and K951-Ac interacted more frequently with other residues in the same chain as opposed to the opposite chain.
source: Acetylation of K951 had three effects on the structure of the tail. First, contacts made by K951 were altered: the frequency of salt bridge formation with Glu residues was diminished and K951-Ac interacted more frequently with other residues in the same chain as opposed to the opposite chain (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: Acetylation of K951 caused the C-terminal end of the helix to become bent and deviate from the typical coiled-coil structure.
source: Second, the C-terminal end of the helix became bent and deviated from the typical coiled-coil structure.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: Acetylation of K951 increased the interhelical distance.
source: Third, the interhelical distance (measured by calculating the distance between Cα pairs in the two helices) increased in the presence of the PTM (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations shown in Figure 7D and E.

claim: K951-Ac altered the electrostatic potential of the S2 fragment, and notably the affected region is proximal to the interacting myosin heads in the super-relaxed conformation.
source: Additionally, K951-Ac altered the electrostatic potential of the S2 fragment, and notably the affected region is proximal to the interacting myosin heads in the super-relaxed conformation (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations shown in Figure 7F.

claim: K951-Ac subverted the local coiled-coil structure of S2.
source: K951-Ac subverted the local coiled-coil structure of S2.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the MD simulations.

claim: The overall motor domain in the K58-Ac simulations sampled conformations similar to those sampled by the WT simulations: the K58-Ac simulations had similar average Cα RMSD to the unmodified simulations.
source: The overall motor domain in the K58-Ac simulations sampled conformations similar to those sampled by the WT simulations: the K58-Ac simulations had similar average Cα RMSD to the unmodified simulations (Table 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: SH3 domains are typically modules of protein–protein interaction and canonically bind to proline-rich sequence with polyproline helical structure.
source: SH3 domains are typically modules of protein–protein interaction and canonically bind to proline-rich sequence with polyproline helical structure (Kurochkina and Guha, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kurochkina and Guha, 2012.

claim: Putative poly-Pro-binding pockets are formed by K58 and K72 as well as K72, T70, T60, S53, and E55 found on the surface of MYH7's SH3 domain.
source: Putative poly-Pro-binding pockets are formed by K58 and K72 as well as K72, T70, T60, S53, and E55 found on the surface of MYH7's SH3 domain (Figure 8A and C).
evidence: This is an inference based on homology to other SH3 domains, shown in Figure 8A and C.

claim: In the unmodified simulations, both putative binding pockets remained intact and accessible to potential binding partners.
source: In the unmodified simulations, both putative binding pockets remained intact and accessible to potential binding partners.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: In the K58-Ac simulations, the uncharged, acetylated Lys alternated between two conformations: a 'native-like' conformation in which the side chain projected into solvent and an 'intercalated' conformation in which the aliphatic portion of K58 was sandwiched in between K72 and T70.
source: In the K58-Ac simulations, however, the uncharged, acetylated Lys alternated between two conformations: a 'native-like' conformation in which the side chain projected into solvent and an 'intercalated' conformation in which the aliphatic portion of K58 was sandwiched in between K72 and T70 (Figure 8A and C).
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations shown in Figure 8A and C.

claim: The 'intercalated' conformation was associated with a disruption of the native contact network among SH3 residues, an increase in the solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) of residue K58, and a decrease in the SASA of K72.
source: The 'intercalated' conformation was associated with a disruption of the native contact network among SH3 residues, an increase in the solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) of residue K58 (partially attributable to the intrinsic increase in SASA of acetylated Lys), and a decrease in the SASA of K72 (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations shown in Figure 7B (likely referring to Figure 8B).

claim: The 'intercalated' conformation abolished one of the putative poly-Pro-binding pockets on the surface of SH3, suggesting that K58 acetylation impedes binding of the SH3 domain to its targets.
source: Importantly the 'intercalated' conformation abolished one of the putative poly-Pro-binding pockets on the surface of SH3 (Figure 7C), suggesting that K58 acetylation impedes binding of the SH3 domain to its targets.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations shown in Figure 7C (likely referring to Figure 8C), with an inference about functional consequences.

claim: Lys 213 and Thr 215 are both located in loop 1 of myosin S1, which is comprised of residues 199–215 in β-MHC.
source: Lys 213 and Thr 215 are both located in loop 1 of myosin S1, which is comprised of residues 199–215 in β-MHC (Figure 9).
evidence: This describes the structural location of K213 and T215 as shown in Figure 9.

claim: Loop 1 connects two α-helices that line the nucleotide-binding pocket.
source: Loop 1 connects two α-helices that line the nucleotide-binding pocket.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about loop 1 structure.

claim: Loop 1 is flexible and is rarely resolved in X-ray structures.
source: Loop 1 is flexible and is rarely resolved in X-ray structures.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about loop 1 structure.

claim: Residues 205–211 are not present in the 4DB1 X-ray crystal structure and thus were built into the structural model prior to performing simulations.
source: Residues 205–211 are not present in the 4DB1 X-ray crystal structure and thus were built into our structural model prior to performing our simulations.
evidence: This describes the model building process for the MD simulations.

claim: In the unmodified simulations of PTMs, T215 retained its crystallographic role as a helix capping residue and the crystallographic interactions between T215, D218, and Q219 were preserved.
source: In the unmodified simulations of PTMs, T215 retained its crystallographic role as a helix capping residue and the crystallographic interactions between T215, D218, and Q219 were preserved.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: In the unmodified simulations, K213 formed a transient salt bridge with D337, transient hydrogen bonds with N334, and transient hydrophobic interactions with V338.
source: K213 formed a transient salt bridge with D337, transient hydrogen bonds with N334, and transient hydrophobic interactions with V338 (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations shown in Figure 9A.

claim: In the unmodified simulations, interactions by K213 tethered the C-terminal end of loop 1 to the upper 50 kDa domain.
source: These interactions tethered the C-terminal end of loop 1 to the upper 50 kDa domain.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: Residue–residue interactions were altered in the K213-Ac/T215-P simulations.
source: Residue–residue interactions were altered in the K213-Ac/T215-P simulations.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: In the K213-Ac/T215-P simulations, K213 lost interactions with N334/D337 in the upper 50 kDa domain and instead formed interactions with T215.
source: K213 lost interactions with N334/D337 in the upper 50 kDa domain and instead formed interactions with T215.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: In the K213-Ac/T215-P simulations, T215-P gained interactions with R204 and K206.
source: T215-P gained interactions with R204 and K206.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: The altered amino acid interactions caused loop 1 to sample from a distinct conformational ensemble in the PTM simulations: it formed a more compact structure that involved more interactions with other loop 1 residues as opposed to an extended conformation with interactions to other regions of myosin.
source: The altered amino acid interactions caused loop 1 to sample from a distinct conformational ensemble in the PTM simulations: it formed a more compact structure that involved more interactions with other loop 1 residues as opposed to an extended conformation with interactions to other regions of myosin.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: The identified phosphorylation and acetylation PTMs are present on β-MHC in nondiseased human hearts.
source: Our study shows that the identified phosphorylation and acetylation PTMs are present on β-MHC in nondiseased human hearts.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: The presence of PTMs on β-MHC may fine-tune its function, altering the dynamics of some myosin motors in the cardiac sarcomere.
source: The presence of PTMs on β-MHC may fine-tune its function, altering the dynamics of some myosin motors in the cardiac sarcomere.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the findings.

claim: The presence of PTMs on cardiac β-MHC in nondiseased hearts suggests they may contribute to the normal functional and contractile state of the protein and muscle filaments that contain them.
source: Therefore, the presence of PTMs on cardiac β-MHC in nondiseased hearts suggests they may contribute to the normal functional and contractile state of the protein and muscle filaments that contain them.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the findings.

claim: It is reasonable to propose that the observed reduction in acetylation at K951 may be associated with declining myocardial function.
source: It is reasonable to propose that the observed reduction in acetylation at K951 may be associated with declining myocardial function.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the findings.

claim: Simulations suggest that acetylation of K951 disrupts the native structure of the coiled-coil and increases flexibility within the tail.
source: Our simulations suggest that acetylation of K951 disrupts the native structure of the coiled-coil and increases flexibility within the tail.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the MD simulations.

claim: Increased tail flexibility may alter the orientation of myosin heads relative to the thin filament, alter association rates between the thick and thin filament, and may affect the ability of myosin to form the interacting heads motif.
source: Increased tail flexibility may alter the orientation of myosin heads relative to the thin filament, alter association rates between the thick and thin filament, and may affect the ability of myosin to form the interacting heads motif.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the MD simulation results.

claim: Acetylation of K1195 may result in similar effects to K951-Ac.
source: Acetylation of K1195 may result in similar effects.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the similar location of K1195 in the tail region.

claim: PTM of the tail region may further modulate tail flexibility or the assembly of the myosin rod.
source: PTM of this region may further modulate tail flexibility or the assembly of the myosin rod (Taylor et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative inference supported by a citation to Taylor et al., 2015.

claim: There are distinct differences in β-MHC acetylation that seem to be influenced more by location of the lysine than the type of heart disease (I-HF and NI-HF).
source: In our study, we see distinct differences in β-MHC acetylation that seem to be influenced more by location of the lysine than the type of heart disease (I-HF and NI-HF).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data patterns observed in the study.

claim: The rod region is perhaps the more conformationally consistent portion of the myosin protein that is accessible to HATs but also HDACs.
source: The rod region is perhaps the more conformationally consistent portion of the myosin protein that is accessible to HATs but also HDACs.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural considerations.

claim: One interpretation of the tendency for lower acetylation of K951 (p<0.05) and K1195 (not significant) in the failing heart samples is that they are not in the globular domain and may be more accessible to HDACs.
source: Therefore, one interpretation of the tendency for lower acetylation of K951 (p<0.05) and K1195 (not significant) in the failing heart samples is that they are not in the globular domain and may be more accessible to HDACs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data patterns observed in the study.

claim: Class I HDACs promote pathological cardiac hypertrophy, while class IIa HDACs suppress cardiac hypertrophy.
source: Class I HDACs promote pathological cardiac hypertrophy, while class IIa HDACs suppress cardiac hypertrophy (Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2012.

claim: Class II HDAC4 has been shown to be associated with the sarcomere.
source: Interestingly, class II HDAC4 has been shown to be associated with the sarcomere (Samant et al., 2015; Gupta et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Samant et al., 2015 and Gupta et al., 2008.

claim: Increased cardiac Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent kinase II (CaMKII) expression and activity plays a role in heart failure development and progression by increasing class I HDAC activity.
source: Increased cardiac Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent kinase II (CaMKII) expression and activity plays a role in heart failure development and progression by increasing class I HDAC activity (Anderson et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Anderson et al., 2011 and Zhang et al., 2020.

claim: Administration of the HDAC inhibitor ITF2357 (Givinostat) improved heart relaxation in heart failure in rodent models with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) by promoting myofibril relaxation.
source: Administration of the HDAC inhibitor ITF2357 (Givinostat) improved heart relaxation in heart failure in rodent models with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) by promoting myofibril relaxation (Jeong et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jeong et al., 2018.

claim: HDAC inhibitors are beneficial to cardiac function by targeting cytosolic and sarcomeric proteins by improving muscle contractility and relaxation as well as cardioprotection during ischemia/reperfusion injury by promoting autophagy.
source: HDAC inhibitors are beneficial to cardiac function by targeting cytosolic and sarcomeric proteins by improving muscle contractility (Demos-Davies et al., 2014) and relaxation (Jeong et al., 2018) as well as cardioprotection during ischemia/reperfusion injury by promoting autophagy (Xie et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Demos-Davies et al., 2014; Jeong et al., 2018; and Xie et al., 2021.

claim: K58 acetylation is markedly reduced in the I-HF hearts.
source: K58 acetylation is markedly reduced in the I-HF hearts, and its localization near the SH3 domain may also be slightly more exposed, with potentially greater HDAC activity in ischemic hearts.
evidence: This is a finding from the quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: The other acetylated residues K34 and K429 are located further into the interior of the myosin head and may be less affected by increased HDAC activity in diseased hearts.
source: The other acetylated residues K34 and K429 are located further into the interior of the myosin head and may be less affected by increased HDAC activity in diseased hearts.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural location of these PTMs.

claim: Preservation of acetylated lysines in β-MHC may be beneficial to normal heart function, and pathological conditions favoring greater HDAC activation may disrupt crucial constitutively acetylated residues hastening heart failure development.
source: Preservation of acetylated lysines in β-MHC may be beneficial to normal heart function, and pathological conditions favoring greater HDAC activation may disrupt crucial constitutively acetylated residues hastening heart failure development.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the findings.

claim: The K58-Ac simulations indicated that K58-Ac caused minimal structural perturbations overall compared to the nonmodified protein.
source: The K58-Ac simulations indicated that K58-Ac caused minimal structural perturbations overall compared to the nonmodified protein.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: The greatest impact of K58-Ac is the decrease in electrostatic potential and structure on the outer surface of the SH3 domain.
source: Instead, the greatest impact of K58-Ac is the decrease in electrostatic potential and structure on the outer surface of the SH3 domain.
evidence: This is a finding from the MD simulations.

claim: Lowey et al. and others have provided evidence that an interaction between the ELC and actin is mediated by the SH3 domain of myosin S1.
source: Lowey et al. and others have provided evidence that an interaction between the ELC and actin is mediated by the SH3 domain of myosin S1 (Lowey et al., 2007, Aydt et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lowey et al., 2007 and Aydt et al., 2007.

claim: K58-Ac has the potential to impede interactions between the ELC and SH3-like domains, thereby reducing interaction between the ELC N-terminus of actin filaments and effectively increasing shortening velocity.
source: In light of this, our simulations suggest that K58-Ac has the potential to impede interactions between the ELC and SH3-like domains, thereby reducing interaction between the ELC N-terminus of actin filaments and effectively increasing shortening velocity.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the MD simulation results and cited literature.

claim: K58-Ac may provide a reversible means to decrease the electrostatic potential of the SH3 domain surface, which may alter its interactions/affinity for ELC and perhaps other sarcomeric regulatory proteins.
source: We suggest that K58-Ac may provide a reversible means to decrease the electrostatic potential of the SH3 domain surface, which may alter its interactions/affinity for ELC and perhaps other sarcomeric regulatory proteins.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the MD simulation results.

claim: A set of studies on loop 1 sequences demonstrated that the length and composition of loop 1 regulate ADP release: shorter loops were associated with decreased ATPase activity, sliding velocity in in vitro motility assays, and preferential binding of ADP relative to ATP.
source: A set of studies on loop 1 sequences (Decarreau et al., 2011; Sweeney et al., 1998) demonstrated that the length and composition of loop 1 regulate ADP release: shorter loops were associated with decreased ATPase activity, sliding velocity in in vitro motility assays, and preferential binding of ADP relative to ATP.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Decarreau et al., 2011 and Sweeney et al., 1998.

claim: In the simulations, the modified loop 1 formed a more compact structure and it is predicted that these PTMs would effectively behave as shorter loops that stabilize ADP.
source: In our simulations, the modified loop 1 formed a more compact structure and we predict that these PTMs would effectively behave as shorter loops that stabilize ADP.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the MD simulation results and cited literature.

claim: These structural perturbations in the ATP-binding pocket could alter the ADP-release rate.
source: We speculate that these structural perturbations in the ATP-binding pocket could alter the ADP-release rate.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the MD simulation results.

claim: Several studies have provided insight on how phosphorylation of cardiac sarcomeric proteins alters myofilament performance.
source: Several studies have provided insight on how phosphorylation of cardiac sarcomeric proteins alters myofilament performance (Kawai et al., 2017; Sadayappan et al., 2006; Wijnker et al., 2014; Kuster et al., 2012; Solaro and Kobayashi, 2011; Yamasaki et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Kawai et al. utilized LC-MS and found that the rod region of α-MHC (predominant myosin isoform in the adult mouse heart) was hypophosphorylated in the HCM-linked cTnC-A8V mouse model, leading to perturbed cross-bridge kinetics.
source: Kawai et al. utilized LC-MS and found that the rod region of α-MHC (predominant myosin isoform in the adult mouse heart) was hypophosphorylated in the HCM-linked cTnC-A8V mouse model, leading to perturbed cross-bridge kinetics (Kawai et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kawai et al., 2017.

claim: Phosphorylation of myofilament proteins by PKCβII and PKA influences length-dependent prolongation of heart muscle relaxation.
source: Incidentally, phosphorylation of myofilament proteins by PKCβII and PKA influences length-dependent prolongation of heart muscle relaxation (Monasky et al., 2010; Monasky et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Monasky et al., 2010 and Monasky et al., 2008.

claim: Sarcomeric protein phosphorylation is regulated by reactive oxygen species (ROS), whereby oxidative stress tends to increase protein phosphorylation due to inhibition of protein phosphatase activation and stimulation of protein kinases.
source: Moreover, sarcomeric protein phosphorylation is regulated by reactive oxygen species (ROS), whereby oxidative stress tends to increase protein phosphorylation due to inhibition of protein phosphatase activation and stimulation of protein kinases (Sumandea and Steinberg, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sumandea and Steinberg, 2011.

claim: Crosstalk between PTMs may provide a higher order of regulation, for example, same-site competition, structural changes in secondary sites that make it more accessible for modification by other PTMs, or direct modification of the modification of a secondary PTM.
source: Crosstalk between PTMs may in fact provide a higher order of regulation, for example, same-site competition, structural changes in secondary sites that make it more accessible for modification by other PTMs, or direct modification of the modification of a secondary PTM (Liddy et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Liddy et al., 2013.

claim: There are numerous pathogenic variants in human cardiac slowing β-MHC, the predominant isoform in the myocardial ventricles.
source: There are numerous pathogenic variants in human cardiac slowing β-MHC, the predominant isoform in the myocardial ventricles.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about cardiac myosin variants.

claim: MYH7 variants are implicated in roughly one-third of diagnosed familial HCM cases.
source: MYH7 variants are implicated in roughly one-third of diagnosed familial HCM cases (Ho et al., 2018) and 10% of familial DCM cases (Kamisago et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ho et al., 2018 and Kamisago et al., 2000.

claim: MYH7 variants are implicated in 10% of familial DCM cases.
source: MYH7 variants are implicated in roughly one-third of diagnosed familial HCM cases (Ho et al., 2018) and 10% of familial DCM cases (Kamisago et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kamisago et al., 2000.

claim: DCM-linked variants T412N in the head region and R1193S in the tail domain may impact actin–myosin interactions or impair myosin rod structure and assembly.
source: In this study, we compared the impact of cardiomyopathic variants located in the same region as the PTMs we identified, for example, DCM-linked variants T412N in the head region and R1193S in the tail domain (Villard et al., 2005). These variants may impact actin–myosin interactions or impair myosin rod structure and assembly (Villard et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Villard et al., 2005.

claim: The PTMs K58-Ac, S210-P/T215-P, and K429-Ac are located in close proximity to pathogenic variants and are present under nondiseased conditions and tend to decrease in heart failure in most cases with a significant decrease in K951-Ac.
source: Additionally, we show that the PTMs K58-Ac, S210-P/T215-P, and K429-Ac are located in close proximity to pathogenic variants and are present under nondiseased conditions and tend to decrease in heart failure in most cases with a significant decrease in K951-Ac.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the study.

claim: Novel PTMs were identified on β-MHC in nonfailing and failing human hearts.
source: Our study identified novel PTMs on β-MHC in nonfailing and failing human hearts.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: Overall, there tended to be less PTM abundance in the heart failure conditions examined, which may be due to increased phosphatase or HDAC activity.
source: Overall, there tended to be less PTM abundance in the heart failure conditions examined here, which may be due to increased phosphatase or HDAC activity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data patterns observed in the study.

claim: Modeling data suggest that some of these PTMs have potential to alter dynamics within β-MHC and thereby fine-tune myofilament function.
source: Our modeling data suggest that some of these PTMS have potential to alter dynamics within β-MHC and thereby fine-tune myofilament function.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the MD simulations.

claim: It remains to be seen whether loss of these PTMs in failing hearts represents the removal of a beneficial, albeit subtle regulation of myofilament function.
source: It remains to be seen whether loss of these PTMs in failing hearts represents the removal of a beneficial, albeit subtle regulation of myofilament function.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future research directions.

claim: Explanted donor human heart tissues were obtained from the Ohio State University Tissue program.
source: Explanted donor human heart tissues were obtained from the Ohio State University Tissue program.
evidence: This describes the source of the experimental materials.

claim: The de-identified samples were obtained from patients that were 41–69 years of age with I-HF or NI-HF, and healthy donors after informed consent.
source: The de-identified samples were obtained from patients that were 41–69 years of age with I-HF or NI-HF, and healthy donors after informed consent.
evidence: This describes the experimental design and ethical procedures.

claim: Human heart tissue was homogenized in Laemmli buffer and separated by SDS-PAGE (12 %), stained with Coomassie blue, and bands that corresponded to β-MHC (~223 kD) were excised.
source: Human heart tissue was homogenized in Laemmli buffer and separated by SDS-PAGE (12 %), stained with Coomassie blue, and bands that corresponded to β-MHC (~223 kD) were excised as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used.

claim: In-gel digests were performed for each excised sample using the ProteoExtract All-in-One Trypsin Digestion Kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
source: In-gel digests were performed for each excised sample using the ProteoExtract All-in-One Trypsin Digestion Kit (Cat#. 650212; Calbiochem, EMD Millipore, Billerica, MA) according to the manufacturer's instructions.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used.

claim: Sample peptides were processed using an externally calibrated high-resolution electrospray tandem mass spectrometer (Thermo Q Exactive HF) in conjunction with a Dionex UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano System.
source: Sample peptides were processed using an externally calibrated high-resolution electrospray tandem mass spectrometer (Thermo Q Exactive HF; Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) in conjunction with a Dionex UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano System (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used.

claim: Raw data were searched with Proteome Discoverer 2.2 using Sequest HT and Mascot search engines and percolator as the PSM validator with species-specific FASTA database.
source: Raw data were searched with Proteome Discoverer 2.2 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) using Sequest HT and Mascot search engines and percolator as the PSM validator with species-specific FASTA database.
evidence: This describes the data analysis methods used.

source: MS1-based quantification of peptides was performed using Skyline 4.0.
evidence: This describes the data analysis methods used.

source: The mass spectrometry data generated in this study has been deposited at Dryad and can be found at doi:10.5061/dryad.s4mw6m97g.
evidence: This describes the data availability.

claim: Starting coordinates for the wildtype (WT) β-MHC motor domain simulations were obtained from an X-ray crystallography structure of the post-rigor, ATP state of β-MHC in the Protein Data Bank (PDB ID: 4DB1, 2.6 Å, residues 1–777).
source: Starting coordinates for the wildtype (WT) β-MHC motor domain simulations were obtained from an X-ray crystallography structure of the post-rigor, ATP state of β-MHC in the Protein Data Bank (PDB, https://www.rcsb.org; PDB ID: 4DB1, 2.6 Å, residues 1–777; Berman et al., 2000).
evidence: This describes the methods used for MD simulations.

claim: Starting coordinates for the WT S2 fragment simulations were obtained from an X-ray crystallography structure of S2D (PDB ID: 2FXM, 2.7 Å, residues 838–963).
source: Starting coordinates for the WT S2 fragment simulations were obtained from an X-ray crystallography structure of S2D (PDB ID: 2FXM, 2.7 Å, residues 838–963) (Blankenfeldt et al., 2006).
evidence: This describes the methods used for MD simulations, supported by a citation to Blankenfeldt et al., 2006.

claim: All 4DB1 simulations were performed with the AMBER20 package and the ff14SB force field.
source: All 4DB1 simulations were performed with the AMBER20 package (Geeves and Holmes, 1999; Tang et al., 2016) and the ff14SB force field (Maier et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the methods used for MD simulations, supported by citations.

source: Production dynamics for conventional MD simulations were then performed using the canonical NVT ensemble with an 8 Å nonbonded cutoff and 2 fs time step.
evidence: This describes the methods used for MD simulations.

source: Simulations were run in triplicate for 500 ns each.
